div.div:
Why this costs a header read per page
scaledPage() is called in full, but every libvips operation it
builds is lazy: constructing them settles the output dimensions
and reads the header, and nothing is decoded until a consumer
pulls a pixel. This function only ever reads .width()/.height()
off the result, so no pixel is ever pulled.
That is what makes the numbers the RENDER's own, rather than
arithmetic that could drift from it.

switch.text: Why this costs a header read per page...

div.div:
One bad page must not cost the other ninety-nine
The per-page try/catch is why this never throws for a bad file.
A page that cannot be read comes back with readable = false and
zero dimensions — exactly as the render skips it — and a consumer
stacking the layout MUST skip those too, or every page below sits
at the wrong strip offset.
